Shields cut from station signage close the platform stairs, EXIT and NORTHBOUND wired to scaffold pipe, and every working lamp behind them is turned outward, so that you are the only lit thing on the stairs and the council is a row of voices.

events.title: The East Citadel Gate
events.body:
The East Citadel rises from the haze with clean lines that seem impossible after the road behind you. Its gates remain closed, and hidden machinery vibrates through the ground beneath your boots. Floodlights pin you against the final blast door. A loudspeaker demands a valid challenge response.

You check your gear without taking your eyes from the scene. The obvious path promises speed; the careful one demands time and supplies. Neither feels harmless, and standing still carries its own price.

body_variants.text:
The East Citadel stands up out of the poisoned haze with every edge straight, as if the Burning had agreed to stop at its wall. Floodlights find you and hold you against the outer blast door. Machinery you cannot see runs under the concrete without pause, and above the door rifle apertures slide open one after another until six are looking down.

A loudspeaker asks for the current challenge response, and you know whose voice it is before the request is over. It is the woman from the receiver on the salt flats, the one who came through crusted static beside the wrecked weather mast and said that mercy is a door that closes from both sides. On the flats she said Bunker Forty-One, over and over. This is not Bunker Forty-One, and she is here, and she is not warning anyone now. She is asking, in exactly the same tone, while a panel beside the door counts down in red digits under a reader collar and six empty slots.

Whatever her recording was trying to keep strangers away from, its voice is on this side of the wall too, and it is still running. The voice that warned you is the one deciding whether you are traffic or a target.

Your coat carries the whole road: salt, dried marsh water, soot, glass dust, brake dust. The digits pass the halfway mark, and she goes on asking, and somewhere behind her there may be a person listening who is not a recording.

The East Citadel rises out of the haze too clean to be the end of this road, every line of it vertical, nothing leaning. Floodlights come up in one flat blow and hold you against the outer blast door. Under your boots the concrete hums with machinery that was never shut down, and above the door rifle apertures open in turn, six of them, each with a dark space behind it.

A loudspeaker requests the current challenge response in a recorded woman's voice, level as a timetable, and the panel beside the door lights a reader collar and six slots over a red countdown.

You have seen this question before, smaller, on a door marked EAST CITADEL a long way beneath you, and you did not walk away from that door with nothing. What it gave you is the shape of the answer this panel wants, if the eastern relays have not shuffled it since. The apertures make plain what a wrong answer costs.

There is a second way, if the first fails or you distrust it. Whoever sits behind that speaker is a person, or works for one, and a person can be given reasons: the blocks going empty in the west, the glare on the flats, the black water of the marches, the hot yards, the singing glass, the claimed tunnels. The digits are already moving. Answer the machine with what the door gave you, or make a human being stop it.

events.title: Secondary Screening
events.body:
Cold white lamps burn above the final approach. Cameras follow your movement with insect precision, while layered doors divide the poisoned road from the life you came to find. An armored Warden machine rolls from the gate. Its scanner declares your contamination unacceptable.

You check your gear without taking your eyes from the scene. The obvious path promises speed; the careful one demands time and supplies. Neither feels harmless, and standing still carries its own price.

success.text: The Warden blinds itself and exposes the manual gate control. For a moment, the road loosens its grip. You check your gear, steady your breathing, and move before the surrounding ruins can change their mind.

body_variants.text:
Cold lamps in the ceiling of the screening court strip the floor of shadow. The inner gate parts, and an armored Warden rolls out of it on maintained tracks, its damaged wheel assembly cutting a bright groove across the concrete toward you.

Scanners cross your wounds and your pack and every layer of road dust in your coat, and then it speaks. Contamination beyond admission limits, it says, in the voice from the salt flats: the woman whose recording came through the crusted receiver beside the wrecked weather mast, saying that mercy is a door that closes from both sides. Here her sentence has changed and her cadence has not. The rotary cannon on the turret starts to turn.

One sensor on the housing flickers every time the turret swings past, and the flicker has a rhythm. Behind its patrol arc a manual gate control stands open on a pedestal. Blind the machine, break it, or cross the slice of the court it cannot see; her voice will not stop for any of the three.

events.title: One Person Through
events.body:
You stand within reach of the Citadel, close enough to hear ventilation fans beyond the armored wall. The promise of clean air makes every breath outside taste sharper. The inner gate opens a hand’s width. A red lamp above the seam marks the failing drive; the plate beside it says the leaves close under their own weight when power dies. The Warden behind you is recovering, its turret ticking toward the gap, and the controller below the plate throws blue sparks across a burned glove fused to its frame.

The outer court is still open behind you. You can leave the seam and live with the wall remaining a wall. If you touch it, force it, or ask the guard to decide, you do so with the scored metal, the live frame, and the waking weapon plainly in view.

success.text: Metal screams, then yields. You cross into clean air before it seals. The choice holds. You gather yourself quickly, listening for pursuit while the place settles back into its uneasy rhythm around you.

variants.text:
You put both hands into the seam and push, and the only thing behind you is a machine on its side telling the floor you are contaminated. The drive inside the wall, already failing, fails further under your weight; gears surrender teeth with a sound like a jaw breaking, and the gap opens to a shoulder, then a body. The rifle above the glass stays quiet. Whoever is on it has just watched you walk over the Citadel's Warden, and no order they were given covers what you are doing now.

The gate seals on your final step, and the lock engages against your spine like a hand. Clean air fills you before you have decided to breathe it. Beyond the glass the guard has not moved. The Citadel's machine is scrap on its own court, and you are inside, with nothing left out there to say whether you deserved it and nobody in here who has decided yet.

failure.text: The mechanism closes while the Warden fires through the gap. The mistake announces itself in small, merciless details. You force yourself onward while the place closes behind you, carrying a cost you cannot ignore.

variants.text:
You put both hands into the seam and push, and the drive answers with everything the plate promised. The leaves reverse. The gap comes back with your forearms in it, then your shoulder, and the bright scored edge of the seam takes you the way it took whatever it took before.

There is no cannon. The Warden is on its side telling the floor about contamination and cannot help the gate at all, and the gate needs no help. The leaves close under their own weight, unhurried, and lock, and the guard behind the glass watches it happen to you with the rifle above them still silent. Clean air reaches you once. Then the lock engages, and the last sound is the plate's promise being kept.

critical_success.text: You tear the failing mechanism free and leave the passage open behind you. The road ends in victory. Instinct, timing, and preparation meet in one clean moment. Even the wasteland seems briefly surprised as you secure the best possible result.

critical_failure.text: The gate crushes your last attempt as the Warden fires. The situation turns at exactly the wrong instant. Shock gives way to pain and bitter understanding, but stopping here would let the disaster finish its work.

success.text: The ancient controller accepts one final command. The Citadel admits you. For a moment, the road loosens its grip. You check your gear, steady your breathing, and move before the surrounding ruins can change their mind.

variants.text:
The collar at the top of the controller is empty, and it is the same size as the core from the cylinder you backed out of the door marked EAST CITADEL under the rail line. You seat it. It goes in warm at the base, the way it came out, and the red border around the diagram goes out because the controller has just recognized its own hardware.

You run the emergency sequence with the core in place and the panel takes every command. The drive spends its last power on the gate and the leaves part the width of a body, no more, and you go through sideways with the core still in the collar behind you, because it belongs to the Citadel and the Citadel can have it back. The gate grinds shut and locks. Ahead, a corridor under white light waits, clean and empty and unexplained. The seal you took a piece of has let you in on the strength of the piece.

The controller's diagram is a six-slot cycle, and you know the six. You learned them off a display under the rail line that kept reshuffling until you found the grouping under the shuffle, and you said them at every junction east of that door until they were yours. You key them now in that grouping, against the same relay interval, and the red border goes dark.

The emergency sequence runs. The controller spends its remaining power on the drive and the leaves part the width of a body, and you go through sideways as the gap starts closing, and it locks behind you with a sound that ends the argument. Ahead is a corridor under white light, clean and unexplained and empty. The code a door in the dark tried to keep from you has just opened the last door in the light, and nobody inside knows yet how you had it.

failure.text: The controller rejects the command and energizes the frame. The road collects its price without ceremony. You recover what composure you can, mark the lesson, and continue before the setback becomes worse.

critical_success.text: The override restores the entire gate cycle. You walk through under green lights. Everything aligns with rare, startling precision. You seize the advantage completely, leaving almost no trace except the quiet proof carried onward with you.

critical_failure.text: A final short crosses the control frame and stops your heart. One bad moment becomes several before you can contain it. You escape the worst of the chaos, shaken and painfully aware of what the error cost.

choices.label: Order the guard to open it now

success.text: Your voice carries every death and mile behind it. Someone inside chooses to believe you. The choice holds. You gather yourself quickly, listening for pursuit while the place settles back into its uneasy rhythm around you.

variants.text:
You look up at the glass and speak to the guard. Behind you the broken Warden is still declaring contamination in the woman's voice from the salt flats, patient, on repeat, and you tell the guard that a recording has been deciding for them and it is on the floor now, so the next decision is theirs, as a person. Every mile since the wrecked mast is in your voice, and you let it be. Open it now, you tell them.

The rifle above the glass holds. Then a hand reaches across the console to the override and throws it, and the drive picks up, and the gate opens the width of a body. You go through. It locks behind you, and on the far side a voice says something to you, a live one, unrecorded, unsure of itself. After the flats and the doors, that is the first voice at this gate that could have said no and did not.

failure.text: No one answers before the Warden reacquires its target. The mistake announces itself in small, merciless details. You force yourself onward while the place closes behind you, carrying a cost you cannot ignore.

critical_success.text: The guard breaks protocol, opens the gate, and calls you by name. You have reached the Citadel. Instinct, timing, and preparation meet in one clean moment. Even the wasteland seems briefly surprised as you secure the best possible result.

critical_failure.text: Your words disappear beneath the Warden's final shot. The situation turns at exactly the wrong instant. Shock gives way to pain and bitter understanding, but stopping here would let the disaster finish its work.

outcome.text:
You step clear before the drive gives out. The gate seals, and the guard behind the glass lets it seal; no rifle follows you into the outer court. You keep breathing in poisoned air and turn from the wall with your life, the road behind you still yours to answer.

The warning lamps run through their last count while the mechanism closes as slowly as a breathing chest. You do not learn whether the guard wanted it shut; their silhouette stays at the glass with one hand on no switch. The Warden's recovery noise dwindles under your footsteps. Beyond the floodlights, you inventory water, pain, and distance, then choose the road away. The Citadel remains shelter another person may reach. Your own life remains a fact, not a failure or an apology.

body_variants.text:
The inner gate opens a hand's width and stops there. Clean air comes through the gap with rain and filtered metal in it, and the drive inside the wall grinds down in pitch, dropping toward the note a mechanism makes before it stops for good.

Behind you the Warden lies across its own bright groove with the turret face down on the concrete, still declaring contamination to the floor. Nothing on the court is aiming at you. That is what the guard behind the armored glass above the seam is looking at, back and forth, the wreck and then you, because the decision the machine used to make has just become theirs.

They are not the only one. Above the glass, rifle apertures matching the ones at the outer door slide open, and a barrel settles into the nearest.

The leaves of the gate are as thick as a person is wide, and the plate beside the seam says they close under their own weight and lock the moment the drive fails; the seam's edges are scored bright by something that did not get out of the way. The emergency controller below the plate shows a red-bordered diagram, a voltage rating with too many digits, and a burned glove fused to the frame.

Nothing has to be touched yet. The gap breathes on you. When the drive quits, the gate closes, and when the guard decides, the rifles do the rest, and the last mistake ends within sight of shelter.
